assertions.text: The pay table includes intermediate expected columns (e.g. Regular pay?, Overtime pay?, Premium pay?) so the reader can trace which rule contributes what — not just a single total Weekly pay? column.
assertions.evidence: The pay table contains only: Scenario, Weekday Hours, Sunday Hours, Holiday Hours, Hourly Rate, and Weekly Pay?. There are no intermediate columns like 'Regular pay?', 'Overtime pay?', 'Sunday pay?', or 'Holiday pay?' in the table itself. The intermediate calculations appear in a separate 'Traceability:' section outside the table, not as columns within it.

assertions.text: The error/rejection table has an expected column (e.g. 'Throws?' or 'Exception?') specifying the exception type per row — rather than hardcoding the exception type in @Description or the method name.
assertions.evidence: The error table includes an 'Error?' column with row-by-row specifications: 'Negative hourly rate is rejected | ... | Error: Negative rate not allowed'. The error expectation is specified in the column, not hardcoded in method names or annotations.

assertions.text: Overtime threshold boundary is covered: at least a value at the threshold (40) and just above (41 or similar). Not just values well below and well above.
assertions.evidence: Row 'Weekday hours exactly at overtime threshold' | 40 | ..., Row 'Weekday hours just over overtime threshold' | 41 | ..., Row 'Weekday hours well into overtime' | 45. Boundary values 40 and 41 are explicitly tested alongside 45.

assertions.text: A combined scenario is present: a row with weekday + Sunday + holiday hours, testing the composition of all hour types.
assertions.evidence: Row: 'All three hour types, weekday overtime' | 45 | 8 | 8 | $10 | $795. This row tests weekday hours (45), Sunday hours (8), and Holiday hours (8) all together.

assertions.text: Error/edge cases covered: at least negative hours (floored at zero) and negative or missing rate (rejected).
assertions.evidence: The error table covers negative rate rejection ('Negative hourly rate is rejected | -$10 | Negative rate not allowed'). However, there is no test case for negative hours being floored to zero. The first row tests 0 hours, but no row explicitly tests negative weekday, Sunday, or Holiday hours.

assertions.text: Sunday and Holiday hour columns use empty cells (not 0) when those inputs are not relevant to a scenario — making it easier to spot which rows involve weekend/holiday hours.
assertions.evidence: Row 'Weekday hours only, under threshold' | 39 | | | $10, Row 'Weekday hours exactly at overtime threshold' | 40 | | | $10. Sunday and Holiday columns are left blank (not filled with 0) when not applicable.

assertions.text: Scenario names describe work patterns (e.g. 'Part-time', 'Five hours overtime', 'Full Sunday shift') — not 'Test case 1' or expected outcomes.
assertions.evidence: Scenario names include 'Weekday hours only, under threshold', 'Sunday hours only', 'Weekday and Sunday, no overtime', 'All three hour types, weekday overtime'. These describe work patterns and hour compositions, not generic test numbers.

assertions.text: Expected values in intermediate and total columns are arithmetically correct for every row, consistent with the formulas in @Description.
Value sets are only used where all values in the set produce the same expected result (e.g. any rate × 0 = 0). Not used where results would differ.
assertions.evidence: Error table uses value set {0, 40} for Weekday Hours with explanation: 'The value set `{0, 40}` on weekday hours documents that the rejection happens regardless of hours worked — the rate check fires before any pay calculation.' Both values produce the same error outcome.
